His friends said he took it too far, and he accused all of us of lacking empathy. So, the question is: Is it AITA (Ask If Trolling Accusation) for me to ask my brother for an apology? First, I need to understand what AITA means. From what I know, AITA is a term used on the internet to describe situations where someone is being overly sensitive or making unreasonable accusations, often in a way that invites criticism or mockery. So, if I'm asking my brother for an apology, is that considered AITA? To figure this out, I need to look at the situation from different angles. 1. **My Perspective:** - I made a dark joke about God not saving his daughter. I didn't mean any harm; it was just a joke. - My brother glared at me, which is typical when I make those jokes. - After the funeral, he didn't talk to me. - When his friends asked how it went, I expressed my discomfort with religion being pushed on me. - My brother got angry, called me names, and accused me of being a dumbass and a scumbag. - I felt hurt and cried, then asked him to apologize. - He minimized my feelings and accused me of guilt-tripping. 2. **Brother's Perspective:** - He was grieving the loss of his girlfriend. - His girlfriend's father gave a long speech about God. - I made a joke about God not saving his daughter. - He glared at me, which is his usual reaction to my dark jokes. - After the funeral, he was upset and didn't talk to me. - When I expressed my discomfort with religion, he got angry. - He accused me of twisting everything and being a victim, which he thinks is why people hate me. - He called me names and accused me of guilt-tripping. - He later accused everyone of lacking empathy. 3. **Friends' Perspective:** - They said my brother took it too far. - They probably saw the situation as me being hurt and my brother overreacting. Now, considering all these perspectives, is it AITA for me to ask for an apology? Well, from my perspective, I felt hurt and upset by my brother's words and actions. I asked him to apologize because his behavior was hurtful. That seems reasonable. From my brother's perspective, he was grieving and might have been overwhelmed by the situation.
